sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy and verification: railroad crossings, light rail and bicyclists

Source tier: every knowledge fact in this section cites one physical page of the official Colorado Driver Handbook snapshot registered for this run (official issuer tier).
Confidence: facts were paraphrased directly from the cited page text; confidence is high for each fact block and no fact relies on memory or a non-official source.
Originality: statements are reworded; no handbook sentence, table, image or official question is reproduced.
Exam facts: question count, passing standard, item format and time limit are not stated in the handbook and remain unknown with typed debt recorded in the exam-authority part.
The bicycle crash-prevention table on the second cited page mixes the words bicyclist and motorcyclist and carries an unclear column heading; its advice is restated neutrally for cyclists and riders only.
The transit agency reporting phone number is contact data and is not restated; learners are told to call the emergency number or the transit agency.
Dynamic facts: rules for riding bicycles on sidewalks vary by local ordinance and are stated only as locally variable; the transit agency phone number is contact data kept out of stable knowledge.
External review: no clinical or legal sign-off is required for restating published traffic rules; none requested.

corpus_stability.reason: Handbook edition DR 2337 is dated 12/05/24 (file Jan2025); its rules are statutory and are not revised more than once a year.
